For project partners, it is compulsory to use the prescribed Orange Knowledge annual report format in order to report on project achievements. The annual report also provides valuable data on the financial situation of the project. Based on an analysis of the project performance in relation to the project output(s) and expected outcome(s), a revision of the project work plan may be suggested by the project partners. The consequences of a possible revision on the project work plan and budget must be made clear in the annual report. Nuffic monitors outputs and outcomes and not activities. Therefore, the main focus of the annual report must be on the achievement of the project’s output(s) and planned outcome(s). The information provided in the annual reports of the projects is used by Nuffic to monitor the progress of the project and to inform the Ministry of Foreign Affairs and other stakeholders about the output(s) and outcome(s) being achieved by individual projects and the Orange Knowledge programme as a whole. Please note that if project progress is in accordance with the original planning, reporting requirements are minimal. Only in case of deviations from the planning, more elaboration is demanded. In the Grant Obligations and Conditions, the obligatory dates for submission of the annual/additional reports are mentioned. The final report must reflect on the entire project period.

actual.value:
May 1, 2021 - March 31, 2022: major milestones already achieved
I. **(May 1-September 30, 2021): remote preparatory work** From May 1, 2021, the implementation of the project was initiated pending the official launch of the project which officially took place at the end of June-beginning of July 2021. So, from May to September 2021, the partners carried out preparatory works which were essential in the development process of the “Field Epidemiology” module. Due to the Covid-19 pandemic, only online support could be provided by Dutch partners in this phase of the project. Thanks to this online involvement of Dutch expertise, the project partners achieved the following: - a detailed analysis was made of the existing modules (epidemiology; community engagement) in use at the INSP - all avenues for enrichment in terms of content that pedagogical and didactic approaches of the existing modules (epidemiology; community engagement) in use at the INSP have been identified - the outline of the "Field Epidemiology" module was formulated on the basis of the conditions specified below. **IMPORTANT NOTICE**: For the purpose of integration within the global African context, and to enable complementarity and synergy, the INSP recommended that Dutch support in the design of the "Field Epidemiology" module takes into account the following prerequisite: (i) the need to align with the overall approach towards epidemiology and pandemics recommended by the Africa Center for Disease Control and Prevention (Africa CDC) of which Burundi is a member, (ii) and to build on the existing course in Epidemiology being developed with support of ythe African Field Epidemiology Network (AFENET). II. **(October 1 - December 31, 2021): (1) design module Epidemiology + (2) consolidating achievements of NICHE/BDI/240** (1) design of Epidemiology module: workshops were organised locally with face-to-face support from three local facilitators (MHPE laureates as part of the NICHE/BDI/240 project) under the remote supervision of Dutch experts. The following was achieved as a result of these local workshops: - The objectives of the Epidemiology module have been set - The pedagogical activities have been defined and designed - Educational activities have been structured according to a weekly timetable. (2) consolidating the achievements of the NICHE/BDI/240 project: the present TMT+ project offers the opportunity to provide limited support towards further implementation of the new PBL/COBES curriculum introduced in the three medical faculties in Burundi. The development of this curriculum needs to be completed in order to 1) enable completion of the training of the students already concerned by the implementation of this new curriculum at FM/UB , and 2) allow students tested positive to Covid-19 and in quarantine to start (FM /UEA and FM/UNG are starting implementation of the new PBL/COBES curriculum) or to continue training in the new curriculum (FM/UB). Specifically, the following interventions are anticipated: i. the design of the final years of the PBL/COBES curriculum ii. the piloting of COBES in the pilot communities identified iii. the introduction of e-learning to enable online teaching of the new PBL/COBES courses During the period indicated, various activities were carried out and results achieved. It is : - PBL/COBES curriculum: curriculum design workshops for the remaining years of the curriculum were organized locally by the Faculty of Medicine of the University of Burundi. Minimal remote support was offered by the Dutch experts. These workshops thus made it possible to finalize the program for the 4th year of the curriculum. - COBES piloting: the 1st COBES pilot was organized for the 1st cohort of PBL/COBES students from FM/UB. This pilot was organized by the FM/UB in close consultation with the Dutch Embassy in Burundi. The Embassy contributed in the identification of the sites for this community immersion training. - E-learning: started in July 2021 and lasting up to November 2021, a series of activities have been carried out which have made it possible to anchor e- learning (distance education) within the INSP and the three universities involved. This operationalization of the e-learning component consisted of:  introduction to e-learning: an online training was organised for a core group of 22 teachers from the four structures. This training was offered online by the experts of the Consortium  acquisition of e-learning equipment: the purchase and installation of the Rapidmooc Studio at the INSP  training (theoretical; practical) in pedagogical engineering in e-learning: a two-weeks face-to-face training for a core of 22 teachers and 3 technicians from the four structures. This face-to-face training/action was offered by the Consortium's experts. At the end of the workshop, each of the trained teachers was able and has developed at least one e-learning educational resource by using the Rapidmooc studio. The developed educational resources have been hosted on Moodle and Youtube for access by concerned students.
III. **(January 1-March 31, 2022): a face-to-face workshop facilitated by Dutch experts to advance the process of setting up the “Field Epidemiology” module.** Organized between February 7-11, 2022, this face-to-face workshop by Dutch experts had the following specific objectives:  Refine the teaching activities of the course  Refine the schedule for the week according to program alignment theories  Practice the implementation of teaching activities  Design and refine course evaluation methods  Design an implementation plan The “Field Epidemiology” module is thus finalized. The operational plan has been drafted but still needs to be completed. It is anticipated that a start of piloting the module could startas soon as a favorable window is found in the current academic calendar. This piloting will pave the way for the validation process and subsequently the start of the operationalization of the “Field Epidemiology” module in Burundi.
